learning_outcomes.text: Explain the basic syntax and data structures of the R programming language.
Implement data reading, cleaning and transformation operations using R.
Make effective data visualizations using ggplot2 and tidyverse libraries.
Perform basic statistical analysis and hypothesis testing with the R programming language.
Apply regression models and time series analysis using R.
Solve optimization and simulation problems specific to industrial engineering using R.
Prepare project presentations by analyzing real data sets.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to R programming and installation
Basic syntax and data structures in R (vector, matrix, list, data frame)
Reading and transforming data (CSV, Excel, JSON files)
Basic statistical analysis and hypothesis testing
Optimization problems and solution methods in R
assessment_rules: The final success grade is determined by the contribution of in-term activities and the final exam grade. The Midterm Examination contributes 50% to the overall Semester Learning Activities. The Final Examination contributes 50% and the Project Presentation contributes 50% to the End of Semester Learning Activities. The overall final success grade is calculated as 50% from Semester Learning Activities and 50% from End of Semester Learning Activities.
bibliography: Wickham, H., & Grolemund, G. (2017). R for Data Science: Import, Tidy, Transform, Visualize, and Model Data. O'Reilly Media.
Dalgaard, P. (2008). Introductory Statistics with R. Springer.
Verzani, J. (2005). Using R for Introductory Statistics. Chapman & Hall/CRC.
